about.title: Covina Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member because of someone else's negligence changes everything, and it's not something any family in Covina should have to sort through alone. California's wrongful death law lets a limited group of survivors — typically a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, and in some cases other dependents or heirs — pursue a civil claim separate from any criminal proceedings that might follow. Covina sees a meaningful volume of traffic activity along corridors like Badillo Street, Grand Avenue, San Bernardino Road, and Citrus Avenue, and fatal incidents can also stem from workplace accidents, defective products, or medical negligence. Whatever the cause, families generally have two years from the date of death to file, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. LawProactive connects Covina families with an independent attorney who can explain standing, deadlines, and what losses may be recoverable — at no cost to start.

whyChoose.title: What Covina Families Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Only Certain Survivors Can File
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents or other heirs if none exist. An attorney can help determine where your family fits in that order.

items.title: The Clock Starts at Death, Not the Incident
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims involving a government entity require much faster action. Waiting too long can close off the option to file entirely.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond the Immediate Bills
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. A civil claim is separate from any criminal case tied to the same incident.

items.question: Does Covina's crash data mean traffic deaths are common here?
items.answer: Recent public-record data shows 117 injury collisions in Covina with no reported traffic deaths for the most recent final year available. Wrongful death claims in this area more often trace back to other causes, like workplace accidents or medical negligence, though any fatal incident on local roads such as Badillo Street or Grand Avenue could still give rise to a claim.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: State law prioritizes a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none of those exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing instead. An independent attorney can review your family's specific situation to confirm who qualifies.
